newsitem.title: USA: i-Pass adds partners for global Internet roaming.
newsitem.headline: i-Pass adds partners for global Internet roaming.

text.p: A private Silicon Valley company that offers global Internet roaming capabilities said eight Internet service providers in North America have agreed to offer worldwide Internet access through its network.

The company, known as i-Pass Alliance Inc, said its partners already deliver more than 1,000 operational points of presence for accessing the internet in more than 150 countries, including more than 525 points of presence in the U.S. and Canada.
Global roaming for Internet access is similar to the way in which cellular telephones can be used outside their home market.

With i-Pass authorization, users need only one Internet account and can use the same user name and password to get local-call access around the world, in most cases paying around $2 to $3 per month for the service and $3 per hour domestically and between $5 and $12 per hour when traveling outside their home country.
Suppliers to iPass include Worldcom Inc's UUNET Technologies, BBN Corp, and EQUANT, which owns and operates Internet access points at every major airport in the world.

The new alliance partners include Digital Advantage Corp of Minnesota, Hawaii's Maui Gateway, MDI Internet of Vancouver, B.C., West Virginia's New Wave Communications, Silicon Connections of Moraga, Calif., Snow Hill Enterprises of Alabama, SSI Micro in the Northwest and Valley InfiNet in Logan, Utah.

The i-Pass roaming service has been in field trials since June and commercial use since October 1996 and it recently received venture financial backing from Accel Partners, Crosspoint Ventures and Asia Pacific Ventures.
